# holtburger-web URL flags reference

Every `?key=value` query flag the web client reads, grouped by purpose. Flags are
appended to the app URL, e.g. `…/apps/holtburger-web/?renderer=3d&clouds=on`.

> ## ✅ 2026-07-11 — USER 1070 SIGN-OFF (docs/1124.md §7)
> Every DEFAULT-ON surface carrying a "1070 eye-test owed/pending" annotation was **signed off by user directive** after reviewing the taildropped local eyeshot pass (real SwiftShader pixels, diff heatmaps; the round-1 all-black `nullRender` trap is documented in 1124 §7). The real-GPU (ANGLE/D3D11), timing/perf, and ear/feel halves are **waived by that directive**, not measured. The 1070 eye-test queue is CLEARED — remaining "1070" mentions below on default-ON rows are historical. Default-OFF flags whose notes gate a FUTURE flip (`portalStencil`, `perPolyCull`) retain their gates.
>

Line numbers are approximate (code drifts); grep the named file for the flag key
if a line has moved. Compiled from a full sweep of `index.html`, `scene3d/**`,
and `plugins/**` on 2026-06-08.

Central parsing locations:

- **`index.html`** ~7590 — `bootParams = new URLSearchParams(location.search)`; all login/automation params + the `agent`/`hud`/`autoLogin` CSS gates at ~555.
- **`scene3d/quality.js`** ~156–169 — quality preset + per-feature override parser (`parseOverrides`).
- **`scene3d/index.js`** — main renderer init; many `new URLSearchParams(location.search)` reads.
- **`scene3d/entities.js`** — entity/movement feature gates.
- **`scene3d/weather/manager.js`** ~30–61 — `parseUrlOverrides()` for weather flags.

Boolean-flag convention (quality.js): `on` / `true` / `1` / `yes` → true; `off` /
`false` / `0` / `no` → false. Integers via `parseInt(v,10)`, floats via `parseFloat`.

## Remote playtest — quick start (VERIFIED 2026-06-08)

The combined cloudflared quick-tunnel exposes both HTTP and the WebSocket bridge
on one origin (`proxy.cjs:7080` → serve.py:8765 `/*` + wsbridge:8080 `/wsbridge`).

```
https://<tunnel-host>/apps/holtburger-web/?renderer=3d&autoLogin=1&account=tailnet1&password=tailnet1&autoSpawn=first&bridge_url=wss%3A%2F%2F<tunnel-host>%2Fwsbridge&server_host=127.0.0.1&server_port=9000
```

- `<tunnel-host>` = the `*.trycloudflare.com` host of the cloudflared tunnel
  pointed at `:7080`. Find it with:
  `grep -aoE 'https://[a-z0-9-]+\.trycloudflare\.com' /proc/<cloudflared-pid>/fd/1`
- `tailnet1` / `tailnet1` is the standing automation account (teleport/Developer privs).
- If a prior session is still in-world, harnesses wait out ACE's session reap between
  boots (s13 inter-arm quiet-gap, `HARNESS_INTER_ARM_GAP_MS`, default 65 s: an abruptly
  closed browser never tells ACE goodbye — wsbridge is WS↔UDP — so ACE holds the session
  until its 60 s network timeout; live-measured s13). `?maxRetries=N` is the opt-in
  stale-session retry.
- Quick-tunnel hosts are **ephemeral** — they rotate whenever cloudflared restarts
  (it has no respawn guard, unlike serve.py/proxy.cjs). Re-grep for the new host.

### ⚠ GOTCHA: `bridge_url` is mandatory for remote, and easy to drop

The login form **defaults to `ws://127.0.0.1:8080/`** (the browser's own loopback),
which never reaches the bridge from a remote device. If you omit `bridge_url` — or
the URL gets **truncated on paste** (messaging apps love to cut at `%` or `&`) — you
get this exact failure cascade:

```
Firefox can't establish a connection to the server at ws://127.0.0.1:8080/.
start_session failed: WsTransport::connect: ws handshake failed
Uncaught Error: closure invoked recursively or after being dropped   ← wasm error-path cascade, NOT a wasm bug
```

The `closure invoked recursively` panic is the wasm's start_session error path
firing on each autoLogin retry — it disappears the moment the handshake succeeds.
Fix = load the **complete** URL including `&bridge_url=wss://<host>/wsbridge`.
(Consider auto-deriving the default bridge from `location.origin` when served over
https, so a bare URL works remotely — see "Possible hardening" at the bottom.)

| `plugins` | `none` | all loaded | Skip plugin loading entirely. | index.html:1321 |
| `nosw` | `1` | SW on | Disable/unregister the service worker (clean test isolation). | index.html:1812 |

> **Stale-entity lifecycle (2026-06-15, always-on, no flag)** — fix for the academy "two leather hats" double-spawn (client-side stale-entity accumulation; ACE serves ONE set, verified on the wire). Two mechanisms: **(1) on ws disconnect (kind=4)**, `entityManager.clearWorldEntities()` drops the dead session's entities so an in-page reconnect/relogin (e.g. the autoLogin kick-dance) re-streams onto an EMPTY map instead of stacking a 2nd set of ACE's freshly-dynamic-guid'd generator items — safe because a reconnect opens a NEW ACE session (fresh per-player ObjMaint → full re-send). **(2) in-session, `entityManager.reapStaleEntities()`** (driven per-frame from the LRU tick in index.js) culls entities whose landblock the player left longer ago than ACE's 25s ObjMaint grace — the retail client contract (ACE keeps the object in its destruction queue 25s and expects the client to cull after, ObjectMaint.cs:41), so ACE re-sends on re-entry. GRACE=30s (>25s) and a wide 8-LB "near" radius mean a portal / PvP dungeon re-entry inside the grace keeps the entity (no invisible opponents). **NOT done via landblock_lru.evict()** — culling on render eviction culls immediately and races the grace. Sites: scene3d/entities.js `clearWorldEntities` + `reapStaleEntities` + scene3d/index.js LRU-tick call + index.html kind-4 arm.

A 500 ms `setInterval` that checks the pump heartbeat `window.__lastPumpMs` (stamped by `pumpNetFrame` on every drain, any driver); if it is stale >1 s — the sole `?singleDriver` rAF pump was clamped by Chrome (occluded/backgrounded/throttled tab) — it calls `window.__netFramePump()` DIRECTLY, i.e. the SAME phase-#0 net drain (poll_events + entity/streaming drain + input) the rAF loop and the `?netDrainHz` interval run, NOT the full render `tickPerFrame`. Complements the always-on 2.5 s wasm keepalive above: keepalive keeps the socket up, this keeps message DRAIN alive so the world keeps updating (previously froze/went barren, and the server dropped the session, on a long rAF stall). The O4-c watchdog (index.html ~9062) only HOLDS the singleDriver claim on a >4 s stall and post-2D-retire deliberately does NOT re-drive the pump — this fills that gap without touching it. ALL added work is gated behind the >1 s staleness check → a healthy rAF cadence (heartbeat <1 s old, incl. while `?netDrainHz` keeps it fresh) sees ZERO behaviour change (one clock read + subtraction per 500 ms tick). `__netFramePump()` re-stamps `__lastPumpMs`, so the watchdog self-silences the instant rAF recovers. No-op before the pump/session exists (`typeof window.__netFramePump === "function"` guard); single-instance guarded via `window.__netWatchdogInterval` (safe across reconnect/re-init); try/catch inside the interval; cleared on `beforeunload`; teardown hook `window.__stopNetWatchdog()`. `off` = watchdog never armed (byte-identical legacy: net drain stalls with rAF). JS-live, no manifest bump. | scene3d/index.js (post `?netDrainHz` interval) + reads index.html `window.__netFramePump`/`__lastPumpMs` |

JS-live for the worker; the companion Rust changes (fixed-cadence `IntervalStream` proactive ping + InWorld→InWorld/EnteringWorld gate relaxation) need the rebuilt wasm. | scene3d/keepalive_worker_client.js + scene3d/keepalive_worker.js + index.html (`__hbKeepaliveWorkerStarted`) + src/lib.rs recv loop |
| `netWorker` | `1`/`on`/`true` forces ON · `0`/`off`/`false` forces OFF (s13 escape) | off (`NET_WORKER_DEFAULT=false` — one-constant promotion seam since s13; **s15 decided NOT to promote**: the Tier-1 A/B (docs/1121.md §4) measured workDelta **+17%** (109 vs 93) AND settle **+24%** (13,765 vs 11,056 ms) on the worker arm — more streamed work per stop on every cold load, not a churn artifact; the only benefit is freeze-survival **8/8 vs 7/8** (§5). A +24% settle tax on every cold load to insure a 1-in-8 pathological-freeze case is the wrong default trade — stays opt-in for bot/agent sessions. Revisit only if A15 residency erases the settle delta) | Transport-in-worker port (2026-07-07 follow-up to `keepaliveWorker`). Runs the WebSocket **and the entire `holtburger_session::Session` state machine** (ISAAC crypto, packet/fragment sequencing, fragment reassembly, ACK generation, keepalive ping) in a dedicated Web Worker on its OWN wasm instance. The worker loops `session.recv_message()` (which auto-ACKs every inbound packet) and pings ACE on its own wall-clock timer, so the session survives even a **fully frozen / 100%-saturated main thread** — the case `keepaliveWorker` (which still routes through the main-thread wasm executor) cannot cover. The main thread keeps the recv loop, dispatch, TickMovement physics, all world/collision/pose cells and every synchronous render read UNCHANGED; its `session` is swapped for a `RemoteSessionProxy` that shuttles `recv_message`/`send_action`/`send_message` across `postMessage`. Movement outbound (`MoveToState`/`Jump`/`AutonomousPosition`) routes through the proxy via the new `holtburger_session::ActionSink` trait. Transferable `ArrayBuffer`s (no SAB/COOP-COEP needed). Transparent fallback to the direct `start_session` on no-Worker-support / spawn error. `SessionCommand`/`ClientEvent`/`EntityUpdate` never cross the boundary (they stay main-thread), so no serde was added. | scene3d/net_worker_client.js + scene3d/net_worker.js + src/net_worker.rs + src/lib.rs `start_session` (armed via `net_worker_arm`) + index.html (`netWorkerEnabled`) |
| `loginDefer` | `short`/`formshown`/`idle20`/`<ms>` | `idle20` (20 s rIC timeout) | s13 (2026-07-11, 1120-appendix A9) — DORMANT knob for the autonomous-login idle-defer. Honored ONLY under `?netWorker=1` (the 20 s defer exists because the direct-path login send is main-thread-starved during the cold-bake storm; with the session in a worker, Connect can fire early): `short`=2000 ms rIC timeout, `formshown`=0 (first idle slot), `idle20`=20000, numeric = that timeout. Bare default (netWorker OFF) is byte-identical to pre-s13; auto-activates if netWorker is promoted. | index.html autonomous-login trigger (`loginIdleTimeoutMs`) |

## Possible hardening (not yet implemented)

The remote-bridge failure above is a footgun: omit `bridge_url` and it silently
falls back to localhost. A robust default would be, in the `bridge_url` prefill
(index.html ~7612): when no param is given **and** the page is served over
`https:` on a non-loopback host, default the form to
`` `wss://${location.host}/wsbridge` `` (and `server_host`/`server_port` likewise
when behind the combined proxy). Then a bare remote URL "just works" and only
explicit overrides need the param. Low-risk; takes effect on next page load (the
service worker does not cache `index.html`).

### 2026-06-23 — ambient swarm fidelity: Swarm trajectory + static CallPES loop (JS-only)

Root-caused from the retail decomp (`acclient.c`) cross-checked against ACE.Server + Chorizite + real `client_portal.dat` bytes: ambient butterflies/insects are **scenery** with a `default_script` (0x33) that does `CreateParticle(Swarm 0x32…) + CallPES(self)`. Two client deviations kept them from "flying around": (1) the Swarm trajectory math was ported wrong, and (2) the static walker dropped the `CallPES` re-play loop, so finite swarms (e.g. `0x320002b5`, total=60) burst once at LB-load and never returned. Both fixed client-side; **ACE stays vanilla**.

| Flag | What it does | Eye-test | Pass criteria |
|------|--------------|----------|---------------|
| **`?swarmAce=on`** (default = **retail-correct**) | Swarm particle trajectory now matches retail `CParticle::Update` (acclient.c:330502-330510): `pos = cos/sin(b·t) * C + t·A + offset + parent` — **C is the oscillation AMPLITUDE** that produces the fluttering orbit. ACE.Server `Particle.cs:160-163` ported this as `cos(b·t) + (t·A + C + …)` — amplitude pinned to 1.0, C demoted to a static offset — and holtburger inherited it (ACE's own Implode case `:169` does `cos*C` correctly, confirming it's a Swarm-only port slip). `?swarmAce=on` reverts to the legacy ACE formula for a side-by-side A/B. `scene3d/particles/particle.js`; headless `test_particles.mjs` (58/58). | Watch town/forest butterfly/insect swarms (e.g. near Holtburg scenery): default = they orbit/flutter with real amplitude; `?swarmAce=on` = they barely jitter ±1 unit and sit clumped at the offset. | Default looks like retail fluttering; `=on` reproduces the old "stuck" look; no NaN/explosion on any swarm. |
| **`?staticCallPes=off`** (default **on**; `?staticScripts=off` still disables the whole chain) | The static/scenery script walker (`statics.js::_runStaticParticleChain`) now handles **CallPES (hook 19)** — retail's re-play loop (`CPhysicsObj::CallPES` acclient.c:318973 → `play_script_internal`). A **self-reference** (callPesDid === own scriptId, the ambient loop) re-runs the script after a random `[0,pause]`s jitter (`RollDice(0,pause)`; <0.0002 immediate) **perpetually** — bounded by anchor liveness (`anchor.parent`) + `_spDisposed` + a cancel set cleared in `disposeStaticParticles`. **Cross-references** are depth-capped (`STATIC_MAX_CALL_PES_DEPTH=3`) to stop cyclic graphs spawn-storming; cross-ref targets in real data are `SoundTweaked` sub-scripts (harmless no-op for statics, which have no SoundTable). `?staticCallPes=off` keeps the one-shot `CreateParticle` emitters but disables only the loop — lets the A/B isolate loop perf (timers + repeated finite-swarm re-spawns). `scene3d/statics.js`; headless `test_static_callpes.mjs` (22/22). | Stand near a finite-swarm scenery prop for >35 s: default = the swarm re-appears in cycles; `?staticCallPes=off` = it appears once then never again (pre-fix behavior). | Swarm refreshes on a loop with the flag default-on; `=off` = single burst; no emitter stacking / FPS drop from runaway timers; no timers survive a teardown. |

### 2026-07-02 — `?statBatchCrossLb` — cross-LB consolidation of the per-LB static batches (Track D, JS-only)

The per-LB `?staticBatch` consolidator emits ONE `BatchedMesh` per (landblock, surface material) — a live 1070 census (quality=low forest, 203-LB ring) counted **~3,008 `static-batch-lb…` nodes**, the bulk of the remaining ~750 draw calls after instanced animated scenery. Materials are cross-LB (MaterialCache), so the same `>=2`-per-material groups collapse instead into ONE **persistent cross-LB `BatchedMesh` per surface material** (`scene3d/static_batch_x.js`), keeping each surface's own material (no texture-array/albedo-only trade — shading identical to the per-LB batches). Geometry deduped per (bucket, BufferGeometry) with `addInstance` per placement; buckets grow by doubling (`setGeometrySize`/`setInstanceCount`); opaque buckets skip the per-frame instance depth sort. Per-LB eviction mirrors `?statAtlas`: membership-tracked gids are `deleteGeometry`ed by the `scene3d._evictStaticBatchXForLb` hook (wired at LRU construction + re-installed per feed; landblock_lru calls it next to `_evictStaticAtlasForLb`), freed space compacted lazily via `optimize()` on the ~10 Hz PVS tick. Lone singletons / LOD wrappers keep flowing to the `?statAtlas` seam unchanged. Fail-soft: any node that won't fit falls through as a plain Mesh; a feed that consumes nothing falls back to the unchanged per-LB path.

|------|--------------|----------|---------------|
| `?statBatchCrossLb=on` (default **OFF** — **CLOSED-NEGATIVE 2026-07-03**: re-feed idempotence fixed (re-bake replaces; tests 24/25) and verified live (instances scale 220/LB across 163 evict/refeed cycles, zero runaway), but the design measurably LOSES on the 1070 at quality=low: rest 26 vs 24 fps (neutral), MOVING 22.5 vs ~29 fps and 1,000 vs ~630 calls — ring-spanning buckets forfeit node-level frustum culling (per-LB batches only draw the ~10% in view) and pay a per-frame CPU walk over ~36k instances to build multidraw ranges.
